subject: Wellbridge prompt-output custody — confirmation & action items
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@wellbridge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap from today — prompt outputs and PII handling

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery call so we have alignment and next steps for your security/legal team: 

- What we discussed: Wellbridge will send a sample data map and three representative prompt flows (triage, intake, clinical-response) so Redwood can confirm what artifacts are persisted.
- Redwood confirmation requested: For each flow, we will verify (a) which fields are stored as part of inference telemetry (prompt, partial response, full response), (b) whether any PII is hashed/stripped before storage, (c) storage region, and (d) default TTL (and retention override controls).
- Temporary defaults we discussed: hosted API (redwood-hosted) keeps inference telemetry for 30 days by default; Dedicated/Private options support customer-configured retention and region pinning.

Action items: 
1) Alex: share the sample data map + one example prompt (redacted as needed) — target EOD Wednesday (11/26).
2) Camila: produce a short one-page summary of what Redwood stores by default and options for shorter TTLs / no-persist (attaching draft).
3) Marcus: prepare a short note on Dedicated behavior and on-prem options for legal.

I attached the draft summary I mentioned (redwood_prompt_output_custody_summary.pdf). Once you share the sample map I’ll annotate which fields we would persist under our defaults and where you can change that.

Best,
Camila
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198

Camila, thanks — received and appreciate the clear recap. Attaching the data map and one redacted triage prompt. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before your annotation: 

- We typically include patient initials and a short free-text problem description in the intake prompt. Our legal team will redact patient identifiers before sending the sample if needed.
- For audit purposes we need clarity on whether the full response (model-generated text) would end up in persistent logs by default in Hosted mode. If so, we need to evaluate the 30-day retention vs our 90-day audit window requirement.

I attached: wellbridge_data_map_v1.xlsx and sample_triage_prompt.txt

— Alex

Attachment: wellbridge_data_map_v1.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet); sample_triage_prompt.txt (TXT)
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@wellbridge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:31:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today — prompt outputs and PII handling

Thanks for the artifacts, Alex — very helpful. I attached an annotated copy of the data map and a short table called out in the PDF that maps the three flows to what Redwood stores by default. Key points up front: 

- Default hosted behavior: we persist inference telemetry that supports debugging and quality monitoring. That includes: request metadata (timestamps, model id, prompt length), prompt text (unless redaction/no-persist enabled), and the final model response. We do not index or surface raw PII in analytics views; PII remains in the stored blob unless you elect to redact client-side.
- Retention: hosted default TTL = 30 days. We offer shorter TTLs down to 0 days (no-persist) as a configuration flag for qualifying customers; Dedicated/Private allow customer-managed retention policies and region pinning.
- Hashing/masking: Redwood can support client-side redaction prior to sending, or server-side masking that replaces known identifiers with stable hashes for dedup/analytics. Server-side masking requires schema mapping (we can help on the mapping).

Sara — looping you in (cc) because Alex mentioned a 90-day audit need. Laura and Marcus from product/security are on the thread to confirm Dedicated/Private options.

Next steps: I’ll set up a short tech review next week between your engineering/legal team and Marcus/Laura so we can scope a retention SLA if needed. Proposed times: Tue 12/1 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 12/2 14:00–14:30 PT — what works for you?

Best,
Camila

Attachment: redwood_prompt_output_custody_summary.pdf (annotated, v2)
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@wellbridge.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T08:19:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today — prompt outputs and PII handling

Hi team — thanks for the note and attachments. A few questions from Legal/regulatory before we schedule the tech review: 

1) For hosted mode, is there an audit export we can request if we need to produce transcripts for regulatory review within 90 days? How granular are the exports (full response bodies vs metadata only)?
2) If we elect server-side masking with stable hashes, can you confirm the hashing algorithm and whether hash salts are per-account or global? We need to ensure mapped identifiers are not reversible and that collisions are low.
3) For Dedicated/Private: if we run in our VPC, can Redwood confirm whether the control plane will still have access to telemetry by default, or whether the customer must opt-in for remote diagnostics?

Finally: do you have a written note on the compliance controls (SOC 2 / encryption at rest / key management) specific to inference artifacts that we can share with internal auditors?

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Sr. Counsel — Wellbridge Health
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@wellbridge.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@wellbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap from today — prompt outputs and PII handling

Sara — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Inline answers below; attaching a short compliance checklist and a sample audit export description for hosted tenants.

1) Audit exports: Hosted tenants can request an export of inference telemetry for a specified date window. Exports include full request/response blobs (if persisted) plus associated metadata (timestamps, model id, route). We can also provide metadata-only exports on request. We’ll add an export option that excludes response bodies if that helps your auditors.

2) Server-side masking: recommended approach uses salted HMAC-SHA256 to produce stable, non-reversible tokens. Salts are per-customer by default (not global) and managed in our KMS; rotation policies are documented. Collisions are cryptographically negligible with HMAC-SHA256.

3) Dedicated/Private control plane: for VPC/on-prem deployments, telemetry access is configurable — by default Redwood performs health diagnostics with a limited control-plane heartbeat; full telemetry collection to Redwood-managed backend is opt-in. We’ll formalize the opt-in contract language.

Compliance artifacts: attaching SOC2-summary-inference.pdf (short reference), encryption-and-kms-note.txt (KMS integration details), and the annotated custody summary.

Next steps (concrete):
- Camila: schedule tech review w/ Marcus + Laura — I’ll propose Tue 12/1 10:00 PT and Wed 12/2 14:00 PT in Calendar.
- Marcus: prepare a 10-minute slide on Dedicated retention/region controls.
- Alex/Sara: confirm whether you want full-response export or metadata-only for your auditors.

If useful, we can include a short MSA addendum for retention/exports tied to the deal (WB-2481).

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
